title: Benchmark launches uranium price assessments
gist: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence launched monthly U3O8 spot and long-term contract price assessments, citing a structurally tightening uranium market. Benchmark projects demand rising from ~74 ktU in 2026 to 98 ktU in 2035, with a 2026 primary supply shortfall of ~4,200 tU that it expects to widen. Contract prices are at a record nominal high of $96.00/lb, above the 2007 peak and ~$6.50/lb above spot.

themes.theme: Uranium demand growth from nuclear revival

insights.claim: Benchmark expects global uranium demand to grow by around a third, from about 74 ktU in 2026 to 98 ktU in 2035.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A ~33% demand increase over a decade underpins a multi-year bullish case for uranium producers and developers.

insights.claim: Uranium demand is rising because governments and technology companies are turning to nuclear power, with approximately 430 nuclear reactors operating worldwide.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Tech-company demand (e.g., for power-hungry infrastructure) adds a new, price-insensitive buyer class to the nuclear fuel chain.
insights.quote: Demand for uranium is rising as governments and technology companies turn to nuclear power.

insights.claim: In 2026, mined (primary) uranium supply is set to fall around 4,200 tU short of demand, and Benchmark expects the deficit to widen through the next decade.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A persistent and widening structural deficit supports higher-for-longer uranium prices.
insights.quote: in 2026, mined (primary) supply is set to fall around 4,200 tU short of demand, and Benchmark expects that deficit to widen through the next decade.

insights.claim: Kazakhstan, Canada and Namibia produced around 70% of global mined uranium output in 2025, per Benchmark's Uranium Service.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Heavy supply concentration in three countries creates geopolitical and disruption risk premia for the market.
insights.quote: Kazakhstan, Canada and Namibia produced around 70% of global mined output in 2025.

insights.claim: New uranium mines take more than 10 years to build, so supply cannot respond quickly to the demand increase.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Long lead times mean price signals must stay elevated for years to incentivize new supply, favoring existing producers and advanced projects.
insights.quote: New mines take 10+ years to build

insights.claim: Secondary uranium supply and inventories, which historically filled the gap between mined output and demand, are set to decline, making the market increasingly dependent on new mines being built.
insights.speaker: Tony Alderson
insights.so_what: Loss of the inventory cushion raises price volatility and the market's sensitivity to mine delays.
insights.quote: For years, inventories and secondary supply have cushioned the uranium market. That cushion is thinning, and the market increasingly depends on new mines being built

insights.claim: Benchmark assessed U3O8 spot (DDP North America) at $89.50/lb and U3O8 long-term contract (DDP North America) at $96.00/lb, with both broadly steady over the past month.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Provides current reference levels for valuing uranium producers and utility procurement.
insights.quote: Benchmark assessed U3O8 Spot, DDP North America at $89.50/lb and U3O8 Contract (long-term), DDP North America at $96.00/lb.
insights.locator: What are Benchmark's latest uranium prices?

insights.claim: Long-term uranium contract prices are at a record nominal high above the 2007 peak and sit around $6.50/lb above spot.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Contract trading above spot signals utilities are paying a premium to secure long-term supply, a sign of structural rather than speculative tightness.
insights.quote: Contract prices are at a record nominal high, above the 2007 peak, and sit around $6.50/lb above spot.
insights.locator: What are Benchmark's latest uranium prices?

insights.claim: Most yellowcake is traded privately in contracts with little price visibility, leaving buyers with few reliable reference points in a tight market.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Opaque pricing raises hedging difficulty and creates demand for independent price reporting and, potentially, financial risk-management products.
insights.quote: With most yellowcake traded privately, buyers have few reliable reference points in a tight market.

insights.claim: Benchmark will publish monthly U3O8 spot and long-term contract assessments (DDP North America, USD/lb) on the last Thursday of each month, based on transacted prices gathered through direct engagement with market participants.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A new price reporting agency entering uranium adds competition for reference pricing used by producers, utilities and traders.
insights.quote: Benchmark will publish its uranium prices monthly, on the last Thursday of each month.
